description.summary: BusyBox applets that need root privileges
description.p: The BusyBox binary is not installed setuid root. This package has a small setuid program instead, which runs BusyBox for a fixed list of applets and nothing else: mount, umount, su, crontab, passwd, traceroute, traceroute6 and vlock. Without it, these only work for root.

trigger.script:
# The applets that need root are links to bbsuid, for the names bbsuid # knows. A name that is free gets one, and so does a name that the # trigger of the busybox package has made a link to busybox. Anything # else is the program of another package and is left alone. # # This does what "bbsuid --install" does, which is not used: it only # works for root, and packages are also installed by a user into a root # that is not the running system. BUSYBOX="/bin/busybox"
for LINK in /bin/mount /bin/umount /bin/su /usr/bin/crontab \ /usr/bin/passwd /usr/bin/traceroute /usr/bin/traceroute6 \ /usr/bin/vlock; do if [ -L "$LINK" ]; then if [ "$("$BUSYBOX" readlink "$LINK")" != "$BUSYBOX" ]; then continue fi "$BUSYBOX" rm -f "$LINK" elif [ -e "$LINK" ]; then continue fi "$BUSYBOX" ln -s /bin/bbsuid "$LINK" done

maintainer-scripts.prerm: # The links belong to no package. Once they are gone, the trigger of the # busybox package points the names back to busybox. if [ "$1" = "remove" ]; then for DIR in /usr/bin /usr/sbin; do for LINK in "$DIR"/*; do if [ ! -L "$LINK" ]; then continue fi if [ "$(/bin/busybox readlink "$LINK")" = "/bin/bbsuid" ]; then /bin/busybox rm -f "$LINK" fi done done fi
